description: Healthcare referral-portal BRD (fictional). Draft-quality document with a direct internal contradiction, an unresolved vendor dependency, two unmeasurable requirements, and one absent decision. The document's own 'Open Questions' section and reviewer comments were removed so the model must find these itself rather than restate them.
seeded_issues: REQ-05 states referrals expire after 30 days, but Section 7 (Assumptions) states 45 days — a direct contradiction within the same document
REQ-02 depends on an insurance clearinghouse vendor that is explicitly marked [TBD – not yet selected], leaving the requirement unimplementable as written
REQ-04 requires notifying providers 'in a timely manner' with no measurable SLA — untestable as written
REQ-08 says the portal 'should be easy to use' with no measurable acceptance criteria — untestable as written
Nothing in the document says what happens to specialist offices that have no portal access (fax fallback during transition is never addressed)
NFR-01 defines availability only for 7am-7pm Mon-Sat; the document never says what is expected outside those hours, and no disaster-recovery/RTO requirement exists
input_text:
Business Requirements Document
Patient Referral Intake & Scheduling Portal
*Harborview Health Partners  |  Draft v0.9  |  Prepared by Priya Nair, Business Analyst  |  March 6, 2026*
1. Background
Harborview Health Partners currently manages specialist referrals through a combination of fax transmissions and phone calls between primary care offices and affiliated specialist practices. Care coordinators report that referrals are frequently lost, delayed, or submitted without key clinical information, resulting in scheduling delays and patient dissatisfaction.
In Q1 2026, leadership approved funding for a Patient Referral Intake & Scheduling Portal intended to replace the fax/phone process with an electronic workflow that gives care coordinators end-to-end visibility from referral submission through appointment scheduling.
2. Business Objectives
Reduce lost or delayed referrals caused by manual fax/phone handoffs.
Give care coordinators a single queue to track all pending referrals.
Improve time-to-appointment for patients referred to specialist care.
Establish an auditable record of referral activity to support compliance reporting.
3. Scope
**In Scope:**
Electronic referral submission by PCP offices
Care coordinator referral queue and status tracking
Insurance eligibility verification prior to scheduling
Referral-to-appointment scheduling
Basic email/portal notifications to referring providers and patients
**Out of Scope (this phase):**
Patient-facing self-scheduling portal (planned for Phase 2)
Billing and claims processing
Telehealth visit scheduling
4. Stakeholders
Role | Name | Department | Responsibility
Executive Sponsor | Dr. Angela Reyes | Chief Medical Officer | Final sign-off on clinical workflow
Project Manager | Marcus Chen | PMO | Day-to-day project management
Business Analyst | Priya Nair | Business Analysis | Requirements elicitation & documentation
Care Coordination Lead | Denise Whitfield | Care Coordination | Represents end-user workflow needs
IT Security Lead | Tom Alvarez | IT Security | Security & HIPAA compliance review
Specialist Office Liaison | Dr. Kevin Osei | Orthopedic Associates (affiliated practice) | Represents receiving specialist offices
5. Functional Requirements
ID | Requirement | Priority | Source
REQ-01 | Primary care providers (PCPs) shall submit referrals electronically via the portal, including patient demographics, insurance ID, and reason for referral. | Must | BRD workshop 3/4
REQ-02 | The system shall verify patient insurance eligibility before a referral is scheduled. Eligibility will be verified via [TBD – clearinghouse vendor not yet selected]. | Must | Stakeholder interview – Billing
REQ-03 | Care coordinators shall be able to view all pending referrals in a single queue, sortable by urgency and date received. | Must | Care Coordination workshop
REQ-04 | The system shall notify the referring provider in a timely manner when a referral status changes. | Should | Care Coordination workshop
REQ-05 | Referrals not scheduled within 30 days of submission shall automatically expire and be returned to the referring provider for resubmission. | Must | BRD workshop 3/4
REQ-06 | The portal shall support attaching clinical documents (referral letters, lab results) up to 25MB per referral. | Should | IT Security review
REQ-07 | The system shall log all changes to referral status with a timestamp and user ID for audit purposes. | Must | Compliance
REQ-08 | The portal should be easy to use for care coordinators of varying technical skill. | Could | Care Coordination workshop
REQ-09 | The system shall restrict access to patient referral data based on role (Care Coordinator, Referring Provider, Specialist Office Staff, Administrator). | Must | Compliance / IT Security
REQ-10 | Specialist office staff shall be able to accept, decline, or request more information on a referral directly through the portal. | Must | Specialist office interviews
REQ-11 | The system shall send the patient a confirmation once an appointment is scheduled. | Should | Care Coordination workshop
REQ-12 | The system shall retain referral records for a minimum of 7 years in accordance with state medical record retention requirements. | Must | Compliance
6. Non-Functional Requirements
**NFR-01: **The system shall be available 99.5% of the time during business hours (7am–7pm, Mon–Sat).
**NFR-02: **All patient data transmitted or stored by the system shall be encrypted in transit and at rest, consistent with the HIPAA Security Rule.
**NFR-03: **Page load times for the referral queue shall not exceed 3 seconds under normal load.
**NFR-04: **The system shall maintain an audit trail sufficient to support HIPAA compliance reporting.
7. Assumptions & Dependencies
Referrals that are not scheduled within 45 days will be automatically expired and returned to the referring provider.
The organization has not yet selected a clearinghouse vendor for real-time insurance eligibility checks; REQ-02 is dependent on that selection.
Care coordinators will receive training prior to go-live; training materials are out of scope for this project.
Integration with the existing MedFlow EHR for patient demographics is assumed to be available via its existing API.
